For most campers I'd get a 250–500Wh unit. The best overall pick is the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**. This comes mainly from one review site, PowerStationGearLab. Its pages carry affiliate links. Wired and OutdoorGearLab returned very long pages that I didn't read, so I haven't cross-checked its picks against theirs. The prices below are approximate.

**Picks for tent and car camping** ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Best overall: [Jackery Explorer 300 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=jackery+explorer+300+plus+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20)**, about $249.
  - It holds 288Wh, weighs 8.3 lb and puts out 300W.
  - It's simple to use and covers phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP.
  - Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is now sold mainly through Amazon and other retailers. The v2 charges faster but has a shorter warranty.
- **Best value: [EcoFlow River 3 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=ecoflow+river+3+plus+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20)**, about $269–299.
  - It holds 286Wh and has a 600W inverter, double the Jackery's.
  - You can expand it to 572Wh with an add-on battery.
- **Best for long trips: [Anker SOLIX C300](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=anker+solix+c300+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20)**, about $199.
  - It holds 288Wh, has a built-in lantern, and comes with a 5-year warranty.
  - Make sure you buy the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC" version, which has none.
- **Best budget: [Bluetti EB3A](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=bluetti+eb3a+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20)**, about $179.
  - It holds 268Wh, has a 600W inverter, and uses LiFePO4 cells.
  - Its app is basic.

**Bigger option for vans or running a fridge**
- **[Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=jackery+explorer+1000+v2+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20)**, about $799.
  - It holds 1,070Wh, puts out 1,500W, and weighs about 24 lb.
- **[Bluetti AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** is another option at this size.
  - It holds 1,152Wh, puts out 1,800W, and weighs about 35 lb (16 kg).
  - The list price is $499. Code AFF5OFF takes $24.95 off, bringing it to $474.05. Dealectric says it tested the code in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21, and checkout has the final word.
  - It's the station alone. The $599 option is a bundle with a 100W solar panel.
  - It comes with a 5-year warranty and a 30-day return window, and you pay return shipping.
  - Dealectric earns a commission if you buy through that link.

**How to choose**
- **Capacity:** Phones use about 10Wh per charge. A CPAP uses about 30–60Wh a night with the humidifier off, and the humidifier can triple that. A 288Wh unit should cover a weekend of devices.
- **Weight:** A unit you'll carry beats a bigger one that stays in the trunk.
- **Battery type:** Choose LiFePO4, which handles temperature swings and many charge cycles.
- **Fridge or appliances:** For a 12V fridge or longer stays, step up to 1,000Wh or more.
- **Solar:** A small folding panel lets you recharge at camp.

If you tell me your gear (CPAP, fridge, number of nights) and budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
